predecessors.name: Spanish Empire
predecessors.text: New Spain's lands north of Central America: the Mexican heartland and the northern borderlands, without the Captaincy General of Guatemala

successors.name: Federated Republic of Mexico
successors.text: the empire's Mexican lands, Chiapas included, passed to the Provisional Government of Mexico (26 March 1823) and then to the First Mexican Republic

successors.name: Federal Republic of Central America
successors.text: the Central American provinces, 'except for the state of Chiapas', declared independent from Mexico on 1 July 1823

rulers.name: Agustin de Iturbide (head of the provisional government)
rulers.title: head of the provisional government

ledger.x: 1821: Mexico declares independence and the empire begins.
1822: the Central American provinces join the Mexican Empire.
1822: the provisional government becomes a monarchy.
1823: Agustin I abdicates on 19 March and the empire ends.

wars.name: Plan of Casa Mata revolt
wars.outcome: The army of Veracruz pledged to restore Congress; Iturbide reconvened it on 4 March, abdicated on 19 March 1823, and the empire gave way to the provisional government.

certainty.note: The page describes the territory as the borders of New Spain and gives no boundary line; the northern frontier and the limit of the Central American provinces are approximate throughout.
